summary: Focused frontend regression passed at 390px: editorial mobile nav now exactly fills the viewport, storm-glass motion layers render, persona/location sync works, and no critical console or page errors were observed. Anchor navigation causes a 16px left visual shift of main content after scrolling.

integration_issues.issue: After tapping Forecast, scrollIntoView leaves .main-content at x=-16px and the hero at x=0 (width 358px), visually shifting/clipping the page even though document scrollWidth remains 390px.

action_items: Prevent horizontal inline adjustment when nav navigate() calls scrollIntoView on mobile; preserve main-content x=0 and 16px side margins after vertical navigation.
critical_code_review_comments: Weather values and partly-cloudy condition remain intentionally MOCKED; no live weather API is connected, as requested.
The partly-cloudy state is hard-coded in data-weather-state; future live-condition integration must drive that attribute and effect intensity.
context_for_next_testing_agent: At 390px, nav.open bounds measured x=0, width=390, y=66; editorial labels are readable. Globe, 14 rain streaks, lightning layer, partly-cloudy state, persona Health sync, Hyderabad location sync, and no document overflow passed. After nav Forecast click, scrollX remains 0 but main-content becomes x=-16 due scrollIntoView inline behavior; retest anchor navigation after fixing.
rca of the issue: navigate() calls element.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'}) without an inline option. On the mobile layout, the target is inside .main-content with a 16px left margin; browser scrollIntoView adjusts the horizontal scroll container alignment, moving .main-content left by 16px while keeping document scrollWidth equal to the viewport. Use inline:'nearest' or explicit vertical scrolling to avoid the horizontal adjustment.
